disharmonies.title: God Classes
disharmonies.problem: God Classes take on too much responsibility,
disharmonies.solution: Extract related islands of functionality into separate classes.  Leave God classes that don't change often alone.

disharmonies.title: Data Classes
disharmonies.problem: Data Classes are dumb data holders that other classes rely on.
disharmonies.solution: Move the data/variable(s) to the same class as the operation.

disharmonies.title: Brain Classes
disharmonies.problem: Brain Classes are complex, lack cohesion, and have at least one Brain Method.
disharmonies.solution: Decompose Brain Methods into smaller methods.

disharmonies.title: Refused Parent Bequest
disharmonies.problem: Child class is large and often complex, but doesn't override or use many of the parent class's methods
disharmonies.solution:
Do one or more of the following:
- Extract the child class into a separate class. Move the methods that are used from the parent class into the child class.
- Make unused protected members private in the parent class.
- If a parent class has multiple children, move methods not used by all descendants to another class.

disharmonies.title: Tradition Breakers
disharmonies.problem: Child class adds many new public methods, but doesn't override or use many of the parent class's methods
disharmonies.solution:
Do one or more of the following:
- Make public child methods unused outside of the class non-public.
- Pull duplicated methods in child classes into the parent class.
- Move methods in the child class that are unrelated to the parent class to another class.
- Remove the child class from the hierarchy.

disharmonies.title: Significant Duplication
disharmonies.problem: Nearly identical code is found in multiple classes, leading to increased maintenance costs.
disharmonies.solution:
- Move duplicated code in the same class into a new method.
- Move duplicated code into a separate or parent class.
- Move duplicated code in two child classes or in parent/child classes into the parent class.

disharmonies.title: Brain Methods
disharmonies.problem: Method is long, complicated, and uses many variables.
disharmonies.solution:
- Decompose the method into two or more smaller methods.
- If part of the method relies heavily on an outside class, extract that functionality out of the calling method and move it to the called class.

disharmonies.title: Feature Envy
disharmonies.problem: Method is more interested in data in other classes than its own class.
disharmonies.solution: Move the method (or part of the method) to the class where it uses the most data.

disharmonies.title: Intensive Coupling
disharmonies.problem: Method calls too many methods from a few unrelated classes (often in a separate package).
disharmonies.solution: Move the calling method to a class more closely related to the other classes that the original method can call.

disharmonies.title: Dispersed Coupling
disharmonies.problem: Method calls a few methods in many classes
disharmonies.solution: Reduce the size of the calling method.  Extract methods from the calling method into the target classes.

disharmonies.title: Shotgun Surgery
disharmonies.problem: Method is called by many methods in many classes
disharmonies.solution:
- Move the method closer to the calling classes (move the behavior closer to the data) if it is small.
- If it is a large method, treat it as a Brain Method and decompose it into two or more smaller methods.

disharmonies.title: Excessive Extensions
disharmonies.problem: Class declares many extension functions across many receiver types, indicating it's trying to extend too many unrelated types.
disharmonies.solution: Consider moving extension functions closer to the types they extend. Group related extensions into separate files or classes.

disharmonies.title: Large Sealed Hierarchy
disharmonies.problem: Sealed class has many permitted subtypes, making the hierarchy hard to maintain and exhaustive when expressions become unwieldy.
disharmonies.solution: Re-evaluate the domain model. Consider grouping subtypes into intermediate sealed classes or using a different pattern.

disharmonies.title: Data Class with Logic
disharmonies.problem: Data class contains non-accessor methods with business logic, violating the data carrier principle.
disharmonies.solution: Move business logic to separate service classes. Keep data classes as pure data holders with only accessor methods.
